name: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport
before:
Kerala's first airport, established in 1932, and the fifth in India to be declared international, in 1991. It is second busiest in the state and sixteenth in the country, handling more than 4.8 million passengers in the 2024-25 financial year.

The location is remarkable. It is only 3.7 km west of the city centre and the Padmanabhaswamy Temple, and about a kilometre from the Arabian Sea at Shankumugham Beach, which makes it the closest airport in India to a body of water. Kovalam beach is 16 km away and Technopark 13 km.

There are two terminals: Terminal 1 for domestic flights and Terminal 2 for international, with three baggage carousels and full immigration and customs. The single runway is 3,373 metres and takes any aircraft type.

It is a working base as well as a passenger airport. The Indian Air Force's Southern Air Command and the Indian Coast Guard are headquartered here, and Air India keeps a maintenance unit with twin hangars for 737 type aircraft.
after:
Kerala's first airport, established in 1932 and declared international in 1991. Second busiest in the state and sixteenth in the country, it handled just under 4.7 million passengers in the 2025-26 financial year.

It is only 3.7 km west of the city centre and close to Shankumugham Beach. Technopark is 13 km away.

There are two terminals and a single runway. Terminal 1 takes domestic flights and Terminal 2 international ones, but the airport lists Air India Express at Terminal 2 for its domestic flights too, and IndiGo at both.

claims.claim: Air India's maintenance unit with twin 737 hangars
claims.wasBefore: and Air India keeps a maintenance unit with twin hangars for 737 type aircraft
claims.why: Who runs it is unclear. AI Engineering Services Ltd, the state-owned maintenance company that stayed with the government when Air India was sold, lists Thiruvananthapuram first among its facilities; Wikipedia calls the unit Air India's and alone describes the twin 737 hangars. Air India's own site answered this session with connection resets (HTTP 503).

sources.quote: The airport hosts Air India's narrow body maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) unit consisting of twin hangars for servicing Boeing 737-type aircraft
